question: The ____________ maestros who revived the art form in the late 1940s include Kelucharan Mohapatra and Raghunath Dutta.
solution:
The correct answer is __**Odissi**__

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The maestros who revived the art form in the late 1940s include **Kelucharan Mohapatra and Raghunath Dutta**.
 
• They played a crucial role in the revival of **Odissi** dance.
 
• Odissi is one of the classical dance forms of India, originating from the state of Odisha.
 
• Kelucharan Mohapatra is considered one of the greatest exponents of Odissi dance, and his contributions have been vital in popularizing the dance form globally.
 
• Raghunath Dutta also significantly contributed to the resurgence and preservation of Odissi dance during the mid-20th century.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• Odissi is characterized by its intricate footwork, expressive gestures, and sculptural poses.
 
• It is traditionally performed to the accompaniment of Odissi music, which is known for its rhythmic and melodic complexity.
 
• The dance form has roots in the ancient temples of Odisha, where it was performed as a form of worship.
 
• Today, Odissi is performed on stages worldwide and continues to be a vital part of India's cultural heritage.
